description: D4 reference systems for Z = 1..36: upstream descriptors (refsys, refcn, refcovcn, clsq, clsh, refq, refh, hcount, ascale), raw and charge-scaled 23-point dynamic polarizabilities, the derived reference C6 tables for all element pairs, the r4r2 values and the D4 coordination-number parameters.

index_conventions.reference: 1..nref(Z), 1-based; matches the first Fortran index of refsys/refcn/refcovcn/clsq/clsh/refq/refh/hcount/ascale and the middle index of alphaiw(:, ref, Z)
index_conventions.c6_matrix: c6_reference[i].matrix[row][col] where row = reference index of Zi and col = reference index of Zj; upstream writes both triangles (d4.f90:230-231), so C6(ref_i,ref_j;Zi,Zj) == C6(ref_j,ref_i;Zj,Zi)
index_conventions.element_pairs: flat lists ordered Zi = 1..36, then Zj = Zi..36 (Zi <= Zj); all values are symmetric under (Zi,Zj) -> (Zj,Zi)
index_conventions.upstream_refcn_vs_refcovcn: d4.f90:174 calls set_refcn(), which loads refcovcn (reference.f90:158); refcovcn is therefore the CN actually used in the reference weighting. refcn is only used by set_refgw to size the Gaussian weights (reference.f90:187-203).
index_conventions.upstream_refq_vs_clsq: clsq is the default EEQ reference charge (reference.f90:236, qmod=eeq). refq is the GFN2-xTB reference charge used only for qmod=gfn2.

c6_reference.note: dftd4 does not store C6 reference values. It stores alphaiw and builds C6 at model setup by a numerical Casimir-Polder integration of the charge-scaled reference polarizabilities. The matrices below are computed with exactly that recipe and are the values the Rust implementation must reproduce.
c6_reference.quote: d4.f90:228-231  aiw(:) = d4%aiw(:, iref, isp) * d4%aiw(:, jref, jsp); c6 = thopi * trapzd(aiw); d4%c6(jref, iref, jsp, isp) = c6; d4%c6(iref, jref, isp, jsp) = c6

integration.rule: trapzd(pol) = sum(pol(I) * weights(I)) over 23 imaginary frequencies

polarizability_scaling.formula: alpha_ref(ref,Z) = max(ascale*(alphaiw - hcount*aiw_sec), 0) with aiw_sec = sscale(refsys)*secaiw(:,refsys)*zeta(ga, eta(refsys)*gc, zeff(refsys), clsh+zeff(refsys))
polarizability_scaling.note: The scaling is element-only, not molecule-dependent, so C6 can be precomputed per element pair exactly as dftd4 does at model setup. It depends on the user-settable ga/gc; the values above are the upstream defaults (ga=3.0, gc=2.0).

symmetry_test.note: C6 is a product of two polarizabilities under a linear quadrature, so it is exactly symmetric; the test confirms that the first index carries no element-order information (the Fortran fills both triangles). There is no 'higher-Z first' convention to recover.

cn_parameters.cn_max_note: ncoord.f90 never passes 'cut', so the smooth CN cap is deactivated (mctc default cut=-1) for the D4 CN; only the EEQ model sets cn_max=8.
cn_parameters.counting_function: count_ij = 0.5*(1 + erf(-kcn*(r_ij-rc)/rc)) with rc = rcov_i + rcov_j (norm_exp = 1)
cn_parameters.pair_radius: rcov_i + rcov_j, averaged only through rc in the denominator

weighting.formula: w(iref) = [sum_igw exp(-igw*wf*(CN-CN_ref)^2)] / [sum_iref sum_igw ...] * zeta(ga, eta(Zi)*gc, clsq(iref,Zi)+zeff(Zi), q_i+zeff(Zi))

secondary_set.note: Global SE reference set that refsys indexes into. reference.f90 declares 17 slots but reference.inc fills only the listed ones (1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11,17). Needed to rebuild alphaiw_eeq if ga/gc are changed.

validation.result: all four quantities reproduced to <= 3e-8 relative for the 9 reference dimers, using only the JSON data staged here
validation.attainable_precision: alphaiw is stored upstream with 7 decimals, so C6 agrees with the official values only to ~1e-8 relative; larger deviations would be a bug
